meta.title: Why Agents Repeat Themselves: A Mini Example
meta.description: A fixture post: Method A stores an agent's workflow as a graph and uses a validation gate to decide which edits to keep, so it beat plain ReAct in 23 of 24 cells.

reader.promise: after reading you can say what the graph and the gate each do

takeaways.text: Store the workflow as a graph so the agent does not rediscover it at every step
A validation gate blocks edits that only help on the training batch

blocks.text: Have you ever watched an agent repeat the same useless action again and again?
The verdict first: Method A is positive in 23 of 24 cells.
ReAct figures out every step on its own, so it easily repeats actions that do not work.

blocks.alt: Left: a knowledge graph; right: a procedure graph.
blocks.caption: Figure 1 — Knowledge versus procedure.

blocks.text: The graph has the form $G = (V, E)$, where $V$ is the set of nodes.
Think of the gate as a checkpoint: a new version must prove it is no worse than the old one before it passes.
